**Answer: 2/3**, from memory of the literature rather than a complete derivation. I could not reconstruct the full proof here.

**Why the value is plausible.** Weak Sidon sets may contain 3-term arithmetic progressions, since $2z = x+y$ is not a coincidence among sums with $x<y$. A Sidon set cannot contain a 3-term AP. So a set built from disjoint generic triples $\{x, x+d, x+2d\}$, with the triples otherwise free of relations, is weak Sidon, and any Sidon subset takes at most 2 elements from each triple. That gives an upper bound of about $2n/3$ on $h(A)$, so $g(n)/n \le 2/3 + o(1)$.

**Lower bound.** I believe the matching lower bound, $h(A) \ge (2/3 - o(1))\,n$ for every weak Sidon set $A$ of size $n$, is the main result of the literature on this question, but I have not verified it.

ANSWER: 2/3
